title: PUSHtap: PIM-based In-Memory HTAP with Unified Data Storage Format
problem: Hybrid transaction/analytical processing (HTAP) systems cannot simultaneously achieve workload-specific optimization, performance isolation, and data freshness because OLTP demands row-store format while OLAP demands column-store format, and existing solutions (single format, multi-instance with rebuilding, or mixed delta-store) compromise at least one goal.
motivation: The emergence of PIM (Processing-in-Memory) DRAM devices creates a new access dimension—CPU interleaving across devices (ADE) versus localized PIM access inside devices (IDE)—that can simultaneously satisfy row-access and column-access requirements in a single data instance without format replication.
method: PUSHtap stores OLTP and OLAP data in a single unified format by exploiting how different processors naturally access data: it arranges rows for the CPU's row-by-row scanning (called interleaved access, or ADE), and the exact same data is automatically available to PIM processors as columns (called localized access, or IDE). To pack data efficiently without wasting space, it groups columns of similar widths together using a bin-packing algorithm, then spreads the columns across PIM devices in a rotating pattern every 1024 rows so all devices stay equally busy. For transactional updates, it uses a two-region approach: a main data region and a delta region for recent changes, with visibility snapshots stored as compact bitmaps written in parallel to all devices; cleanup is done by PIM units when needed. A modified memory controller coordinates all this by scheduling fine-grained access from both the CPU and PIM processors, limiting CPU idle time to 300 microseconds during the load phase of analytical queries.
key_novelty: A single data format works for both OLTP and OLAP because CPU and PIM processors access data along perpendicular directions—CPUs scan rows (interleaved access/ADE) while PIM scans columns (localized access/IDE)—eliminating format duplication and rebuilding.
contributions: Unified HTAP data storage format combining compact aligned format (bin-packing) and block-circulant placement for co-optimized CPU and PIM bandwidth
MVCC support with bitmap-encoded snapshots and PIM-accelerated defragmentation for single-instance HTAP
Memory controller extensions (scheduler + polling module) enabling fine-grained concurrent CPU/PIM access with two-phase OLAP execution
3.4x/4.4x OLAP/OLTP throughput improvement vs. multi-instance PIM-based HTAP on CH-benchmark (TPC-C + TPC-H)

metrics.speedup: 3.4x OLAP and 4.4x OLTP throughput vs. multi-instance PIM-based HTAP; PUSHtap (HBM) achieves 1.4x additional OLAP speedup vs. DIMM at 8M transactions
metrics.other: PIM effective bandwidth 97.4% at th=0.6; snapshot bitmap overhead 2.3% of storage; zero-padding overhead 0.8% of storage; memory controller derived at TSMC 90nm 2.4GHz

limitations: Block-circulant placement and compact aligned format assume a relatively stable OLAP query workload to classify key columns; highly dynamic query patterns requiring frequent threshold adjustment are not fully addressed.
primary_theme: PIM two-dimensional access for unified HTAP without data format duplication
